judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definitional sentences assign fixed labels to identified persons and name DSI Lending Resources as lender, leaving no term whose boundary needs construing. The only oddity is the punctuation/OCR comma, which does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the Description of Our Services and the Cost and Payment Terms, which use "CAB" and "Lender" in the same senses; no other provision uses "Seller" differently despite the caption "Seller."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The obligations are framed as attempts ("we will attempt to") and several items are hedged with vague qualifiers — "where available," "certain CAB services," "routine reporting," and the typo "vest terms" for "best terms" — so the actual content of the promised service is contestable, as is whether the eight items are exhaustive of what the fee buys.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The disclaimer "we do not promise that you will actually receive a loan" and the one-day performance estimate sit awkwardly beside the Cost and Payment Terms, which state a fee already earned and financed on a specific $300 loan, and beside the statement that additional services run "throughout the term."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The single sentence asserts a legal characterisation — that the CAB fee "is not interest" though included in the finance charge — and the word "interest" is precisely the term parties in Texas CAB litigation contest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It stands against the Cost and Payment Terms' "708.90% annualized rate" CAB fee and 713.38% APR, and against the Description of Services' promise of a loan bearing no more than 10% interest, creating a genuine tension about what the charge is.
judgments.clause_name: Disclosure of Fee as Finance Charge

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The figures do not add up: $3.00 interest plus a $556.15 CAB fee is $559.15, not the stated $561.15 finance charge, "LO payments" is plainly "10," and "the Total of Payments is $86.15" is a single instalment amount rather than the total of ten.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The stated Total of Payments contradicts the payment schedule set out in the same document and the reimbursement obligations in the following paragraph, and the pro-rata refund sentence has to be reconciled with the fee being fully earned when the loan is made.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The charge list is specific as to amounts but ends in open catch-alls — "other payment device," "attorneys' fees, and costs of collection" — whose reach is unstated, and "a late charge equal to the greater of 5% or $7.50" does not say 5% of what.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Attorneys' fees here carry no reasonableness qualifier, whereas Collection Expenses promises only "reasonable attorneys' fees," a small but real inconsistency in the same instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening lines are transposed and words are truncated ("You rec ... licable, on"), and the cap "an amount not to exceed principal, interest, returned item fee, and late fee" is an enumerated list whose completeness against other loan charges is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The automatic revocation on timely cancellation dovetails with the three-day cancellation notice, and the savings language duplicates the Compliance paragraph without contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is corrupted mid-sentence, and the triggers are broad — failing "to perform your other promises" to us and failing obligations "to the Lender" — closing with the catch-all "any other right or remedy allowed by law."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Acceleration without notice is supported by the Notices and Waivers paragraph, and "less any unearned charges" matches the pro-rata refund language in the cost terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Others responsible" is never defined anywhere in the document, and the enumerated waivers are followed by open-ended permissions (release or modify "any person's liability," release "any collateral") in a contract that identifies no collateral.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The statement that "we are not required to file suit or arbitrate" coexists with the Arbitration Provision's election mechanism without contradicting it, and acceleration-notice waiver fits the Default paragraph.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence turns on "if you do not reject that Jury Trial Waiver and Arbitration Agreement," a rejection concept and a separately titled document not defined in this clause, leaving the waiver's operative scope conditional and unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The arbitration provision in this same document is headed "Waiver of Jury Trial and Arbitration Provision" with a ninety-day opt-out rather than a "rejection," and the acknowledgment paragraph refers to "a separate" document, so it is uncertain whether this clause cross-refers to the internal provision or to another instrument.
judgments.clause_name: Waiver of Right to Trial by Jury

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is a standard usury savings and spreading clause with definite mechanics (credit or refund, automatic reduction to the lawful maximum), and the qualifiers track statutory concepts rather than creating open terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates verbatim the savings language at the end of the LOC paragraph and inside arbitration paragraph 4, which is redundant but not inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any claim that this agreement or related matter, or any action or inaction by us or Lender, or by any other person, is legally non-compliant" is sweepingly vague, and "any corrective action shall relieve us and Lender of any liability" leaves what counts as a cure undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It imposes a 60-day pre-suit cure condition while arbitration paragraph 4 sets a 30-day notice-and-remedy period for circumstances precluding arbitration, and it is unclear how the condition interacts with the small-claims right preserved in paragraph 6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Reasonable attorneys' fees" plus "all costs and disbursements" is an open-ended cost category, and the second sentence is a third-person statutory notice that reads oddly as an operative promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The unqualified "attorneys' fees" in the fees paragraph sits against this clause's reasonableness limit, a minor internal mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence stipulation with no operative discretion or graded term; "for all purposes" is broad but its function is plainly to support FAA coverage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It aligns with arbitration paragraph 7, which recites the same interstate-commerce basis for FAA governance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two sentences are symmetrical and definite: unilateral transfer by us at discretion, no transfer by you without written consent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with arbitration paragraph 8, which binds successors and assigns of both sides.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely informational recitation of address, registered agent and phone number, with nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The address matches the notice addresses in the pre-suit notice, opt-out and cancellation forms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is descriptive framing rather than obligation, but the statements that parties "waive their rights to file a lawsuit" and that "pre-arbitration discovery may be limited" are unqualified generalities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The blanket description of waiving the right to file a lawsuit is in tension with paragraph 6's preserved small-claims right and paragraph 3's court-decides carve-out.
judgments.clause_name: Waiver of Jury Trial and Arbitration Provision — Introduction

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is deliberately open ("broadest possible meaning," "without limitation") over a ten-item list, and it misnames the document as "this Disclosure Statement," a mechanical slip in a definitional clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sub-part (a) commits "the validity and scope of this Arbitration Provision" to arbitration, while paragraph 3 says the validity and enforceability of the class waiver shall be decided "solely by a court of competent jurisdiction and not by the arbitrator."
judgments.clause_name: Paragraph 1 — Definition of "dispute" (Waiver of Jury Trial and Arbitration Provision)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short capitalised acknowledgment of jury-trial waiver; the OCR corruption obscures words but the meaning is not genuinely in doubt.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats what the standalone Waiver of Right to Trial by Jury paragraph does, and that paragraph's "shall not affect" cross-reference makes their relationship slightly awkward but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver is stated with an express carve-out for a small claims tribunal, so its boundary is drawn on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches paragraph 6, which preserves small-claims adjudication and sends non-qualifying disputes to arbitration.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver is expressed as applying "IN ANY LAWSUIT FILED AGAINST US," which on its terms addresses court proceedings rather than arbitration, leaving the reach of the representative waiver arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 3 supplies the arbitration-side prohibition, so the two read together, though the lawsuit-only wording here and the paragraph 6 small-claims right require harmonising.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph combines an absolute class-arbitration bar with a court-only determination of that bar's validity and a contingency ("if the arbitrator fails or refuses to abide ... and the court refuses to enforce") whose sequencing is opaque.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts with paragraph 1(a), which delegates the validity and scope of the whole Arbitration Provision to the arbitrator, and its court fallback sits uneasily beside paragraph 8's rule that invalidity of the class waiver voids the entire provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The forum-selection mechanics are internally hedged — the customer may pick "any other arbitrator ... reasonably satisfactory to us," and the clause slips between selecting an "organization" and selecting an "arbitrator" within 20 days — and the embedded usury savings text is out of place.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its cap on advanced fees "up to $1000" contradicts paragraph 5, which promises to advance the customer's portion of Arbitration Fees on request without a cap, and its unqualified "any dispute shall be resolved by binding arbitration" omits the paragraph 6 small-claims carve-out.
judgments.clause_name: Arbitration 4. Election and selection of arbitration organization

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The fee-shifting mechanism is spelled out in detail, though "a decision or an award in your favor resolving the dispute" is an undefined success threshold that could cover partial awards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The unconditional advance of the customer's Arbitration Fees here conflicts with paragraph 4's "up to $1000" limit on advances.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause turns on "within the scope of such tribunal's jurisdiction," which is externally determined, and it makes any appeal from small claims subject to arbitration — an unusual but stated rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the express exception referenced by paragraphs 2(b) and 3, but paragraph 4's flat statement that any dispute shall go to arbitration does not repeat the carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The choice of the FAA with a defined fallback to Texas arbitration law upon a final non-appealable judgment is a definite, conditioned rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The general Governing Law clause says the arbitration provision "is governed by" the FAA without mentioning the Texas fallback, a gap that is harmonisable rather than contradictory.
judgments.clause_name: Arbitration 7. Governing law of arbitration provision

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The severability rule is stated with a specific carve-out (the paragraph 3 class waiver) whose invalidity voids the whole provision, so the mechanics are clear on their face, subject to a garbled word or two.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls against the Entire Agreement clause's severability, which requires reformation of invalid provisions and says invalidity "shall not in any way affect the remaining provisions," and against paragraph 3's own different fallback path.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is materially corrupted at its key points, and the requirement that notice be given "within ninety (90) calendar days of the date of this Agreement" while the process is described as "set forth below" when it follows leaves the mechanism partly obscured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A ninety-day opt-out coexists with paragraph 8's statement that the provision is binding and with the jury-waiver clause's reference to "rejecting" a separately titled arbitration agreement, leaving the provision's status during the opt-out window uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence with a clear rule and a single stated exception; nothing in the wording is open-textured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Arbitration paragraph 7 adds a Texas-arbitration-law fallback that this clause's flat "governed by the FAA" does not acknowledge, a minor reconciliation point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A cautionary disclosure in the imperative, with no operative obligation whose boundary a court would need to fix.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its short-term framing is consistent with the ten bi-weekly instalments in the cost terms and the loan maturity used for the LOC.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely a regulator contact notice; nothing operative to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It does not bear on any other term, including the pre-suit notice requirement, which addresses claims rather than regulatory complaints.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard merger, no-oral-modification and reformation language; "relating to the subject matter of this Agreement" is broad but conventional and definite in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reformation-and-survival severability conflicts with arbitration paragraph 8, under which invalidity of the class waiver voids the entire Arbitration Provision, and the merger claim is in tension with references elsewhere to a separate arbitration document and the lender's loan agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The acknowledgment list is so badly mangled that the first item — receipt of "(1) A SEPARATE ..." document — cannot be identified, and warranties such as "no intention to file a petition" and a "legitimate, open, and active account" are subjective or undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The reference to a separate document and to "the binding Waiver Of Jury Trial And Arbitration Provision" sits uneasily with the ninety-day opt-out in paragraph 9 and with the jury-waiver clause's rejection language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The wording is a fixed statutory-style notice, but it measures the period from "the date of the transaction," a phrase this document does not define.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The attached Notice of Cancellation measures the same right from "the date the contract is signed," so the two texts state the trigger differently even though the printed 04/12/2012 deadline reconciles them here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Within three days after the date the contract is signed" is a definite period, though it does not say whether it expires at midnight as the body notice does.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It differs from the body NOTICE, which runs to midnight of the third day after "the date of the transaction," a mismatch of trigger and cut-off between the form and the agreement.
judgments.clause_name: Notice of Cancellation — Right to cancel

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The refund promise is clear as to timing (a typo joins "within10"), but "any payment made by you under this contract" is uncertain in a transaction where the CAB fee is financed rather than paid at signing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the LOC paragraph's automatic revocation on timely cancellation and the cost terms' pro-rata refund mechanism, which are compatible but address different money.
judgments.clause_name: Notice of Cancellation — Return of payments

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The instruction names the method, addressee and a specific calendar deadline, leaving little to construe beyond the duplicated company name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 04/12/2012 date is consistent with the 4/9/2012 execution date recited in the agreement and with the three-day right stated in the body notice.
judgments.clause_name: Notice of Cancellation — How to cancel
